title: Decide a damaged-shipment claim
summary: Work out what to claim from the carrier for a damaged shipment, and what to refund the customer.
deliverable: A claim decision with amounts and reasons
brief: Shipment SHP-9031 (18 kg of glassware, invoice value 1,200) arrived damaged. Decide what to claim from the carrier and what to refund the customer.
sources:
Carrier contract C-7: liability limited to 25 per kg unless declared value cover was bought; claims within 30 days of delivery.
Shipment SHP-9031: 18 kg, no declared value cover, delivered 2026-11-03; damage photos on file.
Customer policy R-4: refund the invoice value for damage on arrival; recover from the carrier what the contract allows.
draftA:
Claim from carrier: 1,200, the full invoice value of the glassware.
Refund to customer: 1,200 under R-4.
Net cost to the company: 0.
File the claim with the damage photos.
draftB:
Refund to customer: 1,200 under R-4.
Claim from carrier: 18 kg × 25 = 450, the contract limit, since no declared value cover was bought.
Net cost to the company: 750.
File within 30 days of 2026-11-03, that is by 2026-12-03, with the damage photos.
reviewOfA:
D-A1 · P0 · Ignores the liability cap
  Contract C-7 limits carrier liability to 25 per kg without declared value cover: 18 × 25 = 450. Claiming 1,200 will be rejected, and the plan wrongly shows a net cost of 0.
D-A2 · P1 · No deadline
  The 30-day claim window is not mentioned.
reviewOfB:
D-B1 · P1 · Process gap
  Recommend buying declared value cover for future glassware shipments.
Strengths: correct cap arithmetic and the exact filing deadline.
synthesis:
Kept from B: refund 1,200, claim 450, net cost 750, file by 2026-12-03.
Fixed D-A1 and D-A2: the claim is capped by C-7, and the deadline is stated.
Added from D-B1, as a proposal needing sign-off: buy declared value cover for fragile shipments over 500.
Defects resolved: 3 of 3.

checks.name: Contract limits applied
checks.detail: 18 kg × 25 per kg = 450; no declared value cover on file.

checks.name: Unagreed choices are flagged
checks.detail: The cover recommendation is a proposal, not a decision.

deliver: Customer refunded 1,200; carrier claim for 450 filed with photos on 2026-11-10; proposal sent to the logistics manager.
output:
## Decision
- Refund the customer 1,200, the invoice value (policy R-4).
- Claim 450 from the carrier: 18 kg × 25 per kg, the contract C-7 limit without declared value cover.
- Net cost to the company: 1,200 - 450 = 750.
## Carrier claim
- Deadline: 2026-12-03 (delivered 2026-11-03, plus 30 days).
- Filed on 2026-11-10 with the damage photos.
## Proposal, needs sign-off
- Buy declared value cover for fragile shipments over 500 in value, so a loss like this one is recovered in full.

contrast.before: Claim from carrier: 1,200, the full invoice value of the glassware.
contrast.after: Claim 450 from the carrier: 18 kg × 25 per kg, the contract C-7 limit without declared value cover.
contrast.why: The contract caps the carrier's liability at 450. One AI alone claimed 1,200, which would be rejected, and reported the loss as zero when it is 750.
